bbs.workflow.reason: The menu owns a merged BBS model; enumeration/find/count use Wren Lists, identity and generations stay attached to foreign handles, sort field catalogs and profiles supply native ordering. bbs.provenance.reason: DirectoryEntry.source preserves all four native BBSListSource values; sourceName exposes the native nullable source identifier as NFC text or MenuError on actual conversion failure. Model-owned source-name storage survives native-list rebuilding and converts only on access. shadowed exposes only retained lower-priority records as read-only DirectoryEntry/Profile views with no cache grant. Distinct hidden-view validation preserves visible lookup and stale-handle non-revival. Native sort records already retain the same full source enum while ordering profiles, covering the fourth ledger row. The user approved removal of the custom DirectoryEntry.type classification; standard Object.type now returns the class. No native precedence, retention, UI behavior or file authority changes.

bbs.cache-result.reason: Native cache_status is secondary optional housekeeping after primary list success. Wren intentionally reports primary success without this status: the user approved that cache maintenance is optional and must not determine mutation success. No cache/store/write-policy changes or new result API are required. Coverage remains Partial because this native status is intentionally omitted; primary result fidelity is accounted separately under model-mutation-results, whose Settings disk-reload and emoji-result subclaims are now resolved by explicit retention and typed errors respectively.

bbs.diagnostics.reason: On request, snapshots copy all four native diagnostic fields in native order, with strict UTF-8/NFC owned names and a lazily constructed MenuError preserving portable status. Overlong section names load with a UTF-8-safe valid prefix within the profile limits and a NameTooLong warning retaining the original section name; values and personal edits/deletions use the original section. The bundled menu opens one scrollable summary for personal/shared warnings and includes web warnings alongside them; exclusively web warnings remain available without triggering a popup. Fatal load and diagnostic-retrieval failures still open their dialogs. Missing optional sources retain silent-skip policy. No public native API was added. Single-action warning dialogs route Up/Down and Home/End to the message viewport alongside page scrolling; multi-action choice navigation is retained. The menu remembers only the last dismissed summary text across reloads/disconnects and suppresses an unchanged summary. Changed summaries can reopen; a clean automatic-warning result resets the memory. Load and diagnostic-retrieval failures are never suppressed.

bbs.refresh-detail.reason: Menu exposes refresh of a configured list but not native per-item queued/active/complete/failed state, phase, received/total/total_known, status and outcome progress records. The synchronous menu workflow does not provide an observer callback.

bbs.transaction-owner.wren: menu BBS model and application startup/connection recording
bbs.transaction-owner.reason: Open/replacement/close, raw borrowed entries, native compare callbacks/cache keys and orphan-cache sweeping belong to the menu model transaction/lifetime. SkyPix honours the chosen canvas and wire encoding, with its configured native Amiga strike supplying cell geometry. A separate optional status row and complete-cell padding preserve the canvas pixel aspect. Wren system CP437/UI registrations remain independent of terminal slot zero. Shared scrollback snapshots retain optional captured graphics, including native SkyPix text and RIP pixels. Scrollback row copies and detached Menu history preserve those rasters as owned Surfaces; the existing Screen pixel-capture workflow can inspect presented pixels. Terminal reset preserves the ring, and row capture precedes scroll/clear. Raster ownership/regridding mechanisms are implemented by the shared native history owner. Its controller-1 pixel format supersedes ANSI tracking requests and mouseSgrPixels reports false for this engine.

cterm.owner.reason: Create/destroy/config service pointers, raw wire writes/decoder feed, poll/finish/disconnect, resize/origin notifications, RIP/SkyPix receive framing, monotonic input holds and native Amiga catalog paths and event routing belong to the active term session. Scripts use CTerm/Screen/Hook/Transfer on that parser rather than independently writing a borrowed decoder or holding output/input/log callback contexts. Screen-mode/Profile policy supplies config values; quiet is a host audio choice. This does not claim a standalone script terminal-emulator constructor. The native configured default strike is borrowed through terminal destruction; exact canvas extents bound graphics independently of complete-cell padding and status. These are fed by Profile and the selected canvas, not raw script pointers. The native ring owns optional RGB pixel strips, released on overwrite/destruction and transactionally copied/regridded with history resize. The shared path applies to all graphics-capable emulations. SkyPix remote-font LF now scrolls host row strips, with off-canvas positions bounded to avoid empty capture loops. SkyPix cursor refresh uses native proportional position and baseline independently of the screen-mode system grid. The terminal owns its clipped sprite overlay, captured RGB and monotonic 185 ms callbacks; generic rendering position bookkeeping no longer masquerades as an ANSI positioning command. Native SkyPix mouse dispatch uses the common synchronized button state, emits exact zero-based canvas coordinates on a new left press only, and excludes status/padding or unavailable pixels. It does not approximate cell positions or fall through to XTerm/RIP encoding. Reports retain ST_CTERM_OUTPUT_USER origin. Native SkyPix font wrapping retains JR-Comm nominal forecasts/counts across input splits and individual glyph commits, flushing at controls/commands/explicit text boundaries. Native EL uses current-font ascent/descent and pixel X; JAM2 blank backgrounds span the font height. These are native parser/raster policies, with no new script methods or Wren-language semantics. Native SkyPix command 22 retains bounded per-terminal five-word gadget records and uses the existing foreground rectangle fill; full reset clears the records. Raw controller-1 reporting remains independent of those definitions, with no new script object, command execution or controller-2 activation.

Existing screen/history, geometry, encoding, suspension, connection/wire ownership, response suppression and native reset algorithms remain unchanged; no extra output/connection status is invented.
